questions.question: Initial antiretroviral regimen selection in relation to baseline HIV viral load.

parts.text: If the viral load is greater than 100,000 copies/mL, what should be avoided?

questions.model_answer: Avoid rilpivirine-based regimens (rilpivirine is only recommended at baseline HIV RNA <100,000 copies/mL and CD4 >200); also avoid abacavir/lamivudine paired with efavirenz or with ritonavir-boosted atazanavir, and avoid dual regimens such as dolutegravir/lamivudine at high baseline viral load.
questions.beyond_mandell: DHHS Adult and Adolescent ARV Guidelines (initial regimen selection); not covered in the chapter text read.

questions.question: Pancytopenia. Name five viruses that can cause it.

parts.text: Name five viruses that can cause pancytopenia.

questions.model_answer: (1) Parvovirus B19 (2) HIV (3) Cytomegalovirus (CMV) (4) Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) (5) Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6).
questions.beyond_mandell: Pancytopenia differential is general ID/hematology knowledge; this Mandell chapter notes only that transient pancytopenia after B19 infection is rare and does not list a viral differential.

cohort_answer.text: Parvo B19, HIV, HHV6, EBV, CMV

questions.question: A neonate is born to a mother with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection who received no prenatal care.
questions.question_raw: Congenital HIV and HBV to mother with no prenatal care.

parts.text: How can HIV transmission be prevented? List two mechanisms.
What two things are given to prevent HBV transmission?

parts_raw.text: How to prevent HIV transmission, list two mechanisms?
What two things are given to prevent HBV transmission?

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Maternal suppressive antiretroviral therapy in pregnancy and intravenous intrapartum zidovudine when the viral load is unknown or >1000 copies/mL (with scheduled cesarean delivery at 38 weeks if viral load >1000 copies/mL). (2) Infant antiretroviral prophylaxis started within 6 hours of birth — presumptive multidrug therapy (zidovudine + lamivudine + nevirapine or raltegravir) in this high-risk, untreated-mother scenario — together with complete avoidance of breastfeeding where safe replacement feeding is available.
b) (1) Hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) and (2) hepatitis B vaccine, both given within 12 hours of birth, with the vaccine series completed and post-vaccination serology at 9-12 months.
questions.beyond_mandell: DHHS Perinatal HIV Guidelines and CDC/ACIP hepatitis B perinatal recommendations; the chapter text read covers HIV virology and biology of transmission only.

cohort_answer.text: HIV prevention mechanisms: ART during pregnancy; C-section if viral load is >1000 copies; Intrapartum AZT if >1000 (or consider if 50-999 copies, no need if <50 copies); No breastfeeding; Triple empiric HIV therapy for baby. HBV prevention: Treat mother 28wks onwards; HBIG and Hep B vaccine

questions.question: Pancytopenia. Name five viruses that can cause it.

parts.text: Name five viruses that can cause pancytopenia.

parts_raw.text: Name five viruses that can cause it

questions.model_answer: (1) Parvovirus B19 (2) HIV (3) Cytomegalovirus (CMV) (4) Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) (5) Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6). (Other recognized causes: hepatitis viruses, dengue/other flaviviruses, measles.)
questions.beyond_mandell: Viral pancytopenia differential is general ID/hematology knowledge; not covered as a list in this chapter.

cohort_answer.text: HIV, HBV, Parvovirus B19, CMV, EBV, Flaviviruses (Dengue, Zika), Hepatitis A (can be associated with transient neutropenia in early stages), Measles, Rubella, HHV6
